subject: general
question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 10 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 12, 15, and 10 = 60 units.

Efficiencies: A = 60 ÷ 12 = 5, B = 60 ÷ 15 = 4, C = −(60 ÷ 10) = −6.

Combined efficiency of all three pipes = 5 + 4 − 6 = 3 units/hr.

Time required to fill the tank = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 12 hours

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the tank = 15 hours

Time taken by Pipe C to empty the tank = 10 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given time periods

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

Total Time = Total Work ÷ Net Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**

 A

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of C

⇒ Net efficiency = 5 + 4 − 6

⇒ Net efficiency = 3 units/hour

⇒ Total time taken to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Rules

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its 1 hour work is 1 ÷ x. If another empties in y hours, its 1 hour work is −1 ÷ y.

Concept of Net Efficiency

Net efficiency is the algebraic sum of individual efficiencies. Inlet (filling) pipes have positive efficiency, and outlet (emptying) pipes have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

When multiple people or pipes are involved, any monetary wages or costs are distributed in direct proportion to the actual work done or the respective efficiencies.
